desc: baseline: unmodified tree, oltp PROFILE=1 MYSQL=1

asi.gap: vitess at 10.6% of mysql qps; single-threaded so latency-bound: ~4.3ms overhead per 20-query transaction

desc: parallel multi-shard commit in TxConn.commitNormal (was serial per shard)

asi.conclusion: no gain vs baseline mean ~5094; expected +5% from removing 1 serial commit RTT but goroutine spawn+handoff on GOMAXPROCS=2 likely eats the savings. Commit RPCs also not counted in VttabletCall histogram so commit cost per txn may be smaller than assumed.
asi.theory_formed: systemic tax is Go netpoll/scheduler wakeup latency (~10-20us) occurring ~6x per query across vtgate+tablet; explains tablet mysql layer 64us vs 24us raw, and grpc hop 95us vs 40us net floor
asi.next: test wakeup-latency theory with env-gated scheduler spinner goroutine

desc: scheduler spinner goroutine (for{Gosched()}) in servenv, env-gated VT_SCHED_SPIN, enabled on vtgate+tablets

asi.conclusion: 8x WORSE. Busy-spin exhausts docker CFS quota (cpu.max 200000/100000) -> multi-ms throttle pauses (p95 42ms). NEVER busy-spin under cgroup cpu limits.
asi.still_open: wakeup-latency theory unconfirmed (test confounded by throttling)
asi.next: isolate go/mysql client overhead vs raw C client with a minimal Go binary inside the container

desc: diagnostic: go/mysql client tight-loop in idle process inside mysql-1001 container

asi.conclusion: go/mysql client is fast (12.6us vs C client 10.3us). The 64us seen in busy vttablet = ~50us scheduler/wakeup tax. No CFS throttling under normal load. Attack handoffs/wakeups, not client code.
asi.tool: .auto/diag_mysqlbench/main.go, cross-compile GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0, docker cp into mysql container

desc: grpc.NumStreamWorkers(GOMAXPROCS) on servenv grpc server (vtgate+vttablet) - reuse stream worker goroutines instead of per-RPC spawn

asi.protocol_change: measure.sh now BENCH_REPEAT=3 within one cluster + median; within-cluster spread ~1%, cluster-to-cluster ±4-5%

desc: GOGC=200 + drop GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB (was GOGC=off) on vtgate+tablets

asi.ab: two independent clusters: 5417 (5279-5445) and 5424 (5398-5424) vs exp5 5288. +2.5%
asi.why: GOGC=off+memlimit causes rare full-1GiB GC cycles with assist storms (10-50ms histogram outliers); GOGC=200 does small frequent cycles
asi.note: env-only change in benchmarks compose files

desc: bidi-stream Execute pipe: queryservice.QueryPipe/ExecutePipe grpc service + client pipe pool in grpctabletconn, replaces per-query unary Execute

asi.design: one in-flight request per pipe, pool for concurrency, error terminates pipe w/ full grpc status, Unimplemented->permanent unary fallback, ctx enforced via context.AfterFunc cancel
asi.caveat: per-call grpc-timeout no longer propagated to tablet (tablet's own query timeout still applies); errors cost a stream re-setup
asi.validation: tabletconntest conformance suite passes through pipe path; 0 sysbench errors
asi.next: extend pipe to BeginExecute/Commit (4 of ~22 calls/txn)

desc: extend pipe to BeginExecute + Commit (generic pipeHandler + per-method pools)

asi.why_no_gain: only ~4 of 24 RPCs/txn; BeginExecute already piggybacks begin onto first query; commit RTT partially overlaps txn end
asi.learning: pipe wins scale with call volume; Execute (~18/24 calls) was the whole prize
asi.code_note: generic version preserved in git history at commit before this revert if ever needed

desc: fastquery: raw length-prefixed TCP transport for Execute (vtgate->vttablet), env-gated VT_FASTQUERY, port=grpc+1, in-band vtrpc errors, fallback to grpc pipe

asi.ab: 7167 (7048-7392) + 6344 (6133-6990) across two clusters vs grpc-pipe best 5747: +17-25%
asi.why_it_works: raw TCP echo floor between containers is 5-12us vs grpc hop ~95us; fastquery removes HTTP/2 framing + ALL goroutine handoffs (caller writes from own goroutine, netpoll wakes caller directly)
asi.validation: 4 unit tests (roundtrip, app error keeps conn, ctx cancel, dial failure); 0 sysbench errors all samples
asi.caveats: no TLS/auth (gated off by default); ctx deadline not propagated to tablet (server uses context.Background); Execute only
asi.next: re-profile to find new bottleneck distribution

desc: fastquery: add BeginExecute + Commit methods (generic Pool.Call, method tags 2/3)

asi.lesson: exp8 (begin/commit via grpc pipe) gained nothing when Execute was also grpc; now that Execute is on raw TCP, the 2x ~95us grpc commits per txn were 7%+ of txn time - relative weights shift as you optimize, revisit discarded ideas
asi.validation: 0 sysbench errors, unit tests + tabletconntest pass

desc: fastquery custom sqltypes.Result wire codec (skip ResultToProto3/MarshalVT/UnmarshalVT/Proto3ToResult layers for Execute)

asi.ab: 8260 vs exp10 8303: FLAT within noise, p95 2.91->2.86
asi.mechanism_confirmed: vtgate allocs 9GB->8GB; per-row UnmarshalVT allocs (28% of heap) replaced by 1 buffer + 2 slice allocs per query; decode is 3 allocs total regardless of row count
asi.why_flat: alloc CPU was not the dominant critical-path cost; syscall+wakeup wall time still rules
asi.kept_because: strictly simpler data flow (Result straight through, no proto detour), lower GC pressure, prerequisite for future row pass-through (mysql text rows could flow tablet->vtgate->client nearly verbatim)
asi.validation: codec roundtrip vs proto-path equivalence tests + truncation fuzz, 0 sysbench errors

asi.risk: GOGC=800 without memlimit can balloon heap toward the 1GB container limit -> OOM risk; not worth an unprovable 1%

desc: bounded spin-read (50us non-blocking busy-poll before parking) in fastquery client

asi.why: each non-blocking syscall.Read is a full syscall (~1-3us under docker seccomp); spinning 50us = 20-50 wasted syscalls per call, far more expensive than the one ~10-20us futex wakeup it avoids
asi.learning: in containers, syscalls are the expensive unit, not wakeups; never busy-poll with syscalls. Wakeup tax must be attacked by REMOVING blocking points (pipelining), not cheaper waiting

desc: retry parallel multi-shard commit (exp2) now that commits ride fastquery

asi.why: goroutine spawn+WaitGroup+handoff (~15us) on GOMAXPROCS=2 cancels the ~60us saved serial RPC; net effect ~1-2%, below noise
asi.learning: on small-GOMAXPROCS runtimes, parallelism via goroutines only pays when the parallelized work is >>15us; pipelining on ONE goroutine (send both, then read both) would avoid the spawn cost entirely - see ideas.md

desc: final verification: full MYSQL=1 comparison on current HEAD

asi.vs_mysql: -82.3% (was -89.4% at baseline); mysql itself stable (46894 vs 46805) so gains are real
